rationale: enc-3des is a small (12.8KB text, 12 functions) crypto kernel whose hot path is concentrated in des3_crypt/des_crypt tight round loops, so cheap data-oriented transforms dominate: SUB gets the highest weights because cipher code is dense in boolean/arithmetic operations it can obscure at near-zero runtime and size cost with minimal correctness risk, and SPLIT complements it by breaking large basic blocks (7425-byte des3_crypt) into diverse fragments cheaply. Expensive control-flow passes are deliberately throttled: BCF and FLA carry high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so the selector applies them only to functions whose features show low loop intensity (e.g., key-schedule setup like des_main_ks, des3_set_3keys) rather than the encryption inner loops, keeping benchmark runtime acceptable in a 644-line program with little slack. IBR is kept at moderate weight to add branch indirection where blocks are not ultra-hot, while ICALL is down-weighted and risk-weighted because this codebase is dominated by direct intra-module calls with few indirect-call sites, so it adds overhead and correctness exposure with little diversity payoff; IGV stays mild since des.c uses few globals, offering modest diversity at low cost. Overall the table biases toward high-SecurityGain/low-cost passes and gates the costly passes behind cost-sensitive weights, maximizing resistance per unit of runtime/size overhead while preserving correctness.
